strengths: The core idea is simple, original in this context, and potentially useful: dense cross-view correspondences are triangulated to initialize 3D Gaussians near scene surfaces, allowing densification to be disabled without changing the downstream 3DGS optimizer.

The empirical results cover 13 scenes from Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending. The 30K variants generally provide strong perceptual quality, while the 5K variants show meaningful speed-quality trade-offs; the reported initialization cost is included in the proposed method's runtime.

The method reduces Gaussian count substantially relative to standard 3DGS and demonstrates complementarity with Taming-3DGS, supporting the practical value of improving initialization rather than introducing a specialized representation.

Ablations examine densification, several correspondence models, monocular-depth initialization, noise sensitivity, sampling density, reference-view count, and Gaussian parameter motion. These experiments broadly support the proposed mechanism rather than presenting benchmark results alone.
Qualitative examples indicate improved preservation of fine structures and textures, and the paper is generally easy to follow at the conceptual level.
weaknesses: The triangulation derivation is technically incorrect or too malformed to support reproduction. Equations 6–7 set b to zero and minimize ||A g|| over an unconstrained 3D point, whose trivial solution is zero; the stated dimensions and transposes of the projection matrices are also inconsistent. Correct homogeneous DLT requires a normalization constraint/SVD, or an inhomogeneous system must move the fourth-coordinate terms into a nonzero right-hand side. This is a material problem in the central method description.

Important implementation details are missing: the exact camera-neighbor distance calculation and normalization, confidence threshold, correspondence sampling and deduplication, rejection of invalid/behind-camera or poorly conditioned triangulations, Gaussian scale formula and coefficient, opacity initialization, and treatment of spherical-harmonic coefficients. Referring only to default 3DGS optimization is insufficient to reproduce the initialization.

The supplementary per-scene SSIM table reports 0.998 for the Mip-NeRF360 counter scene for Ours+3DGS. This is implausibly far above the companion Taming result of 0.925 and typical scores, and it is exactly included in the reported 0.840 mean. A likely typo or evaluation error would materially change the aggregate comparison, so the headline quality evidence is not fully trustworthy as presented.

The experimental accounting is not as uniformly controlled as claimed. The text says competing methods were evaluated on the same A100, but Table 1 mixes reproduced results with paper-reported results from A6000/RTX 3090 systems. There is also no separate breakdown of dense matching, triangulation, and optimization time, nor any analysis of CPU/GPU preprocessing, making the source and portability of the speedup difficult to assess.

Results appear to be single runs without variability or statistical testing. This matters for relatively small differences such as 27.80 versus 27.84 PSNR with/without densification and comparisons among several quality-focused baselines.

Some conclusions exceed the evidence: compatibility is demonstrated only with Taming-3DGS rather than the broad set of acceleration techniques claimed, extreme-view robustness is supported by one qualitative example, and sparse-view capability is asserted from a public demo rather than evaluated systematically.

The method depends on a pretrained dense matcher and accurate camera poses, but failure cases under repeated texture, weak overlap, occlusion, specularity, pose error, or domains outside the matcher's training distribution are not evaluated. The acknowledged weakness on reflective surfaces is likewise not quantified.

The manuscript contains numerous presentation errors—incorrect covariance dimensionality, ambiguous rendering notation, inconsistent descriptions of correspondence aggregation, and typographical issues. Individually these are fixable, but together with the central triangulation error they substantially reduce technical clarity and reproducibility.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical bottleneck in 3D Gaussian Splatting: slow convergence caused by iterative densification. Initializing Gaussians from triangulated dense correspondences is intuitive, potentially useful, and compatible with existing optimizers and rasterizers.

The evaluation covers all 13 scenes from Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending, reports PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, runtime, and Gaussian count, and includes per-scene results. The matching, depth-initialization, densification, noise, and sampling ablations provide useful evidence that initialization quality matters.

The reported efficiency-quality tradeoff is promising. For example, the 5K variants reduce runtime substantially while remaining competitive, and combining the initialization with Taming-3DGS generally improves its reconstruction metrics.
The qualitative results and Gaussian-motion analysis support the proposed intuition that dense initialization can improve coverage and shorten optimization trajectories.
weaknesses: The central triangulation derivation is technically incorrect as written. Equations 6–7 set b=0 and minimize ||A g||² without a scale constraint, whose trivial solution is g=0. The dimensions and conventions are also inconsistent: projection matrices are described as 4x3, g alternates between 3D and homogeneous 4D, and A is not coherently defined. A valid homogeneous DLT formulation requires a constrained/SVD solution, or an inhomogeneous system with nonzero terms. Because triangulation is the core operation, this is a material correctness issue rather than a presentation refinement.

The 3DGS formulation in Equation 1 is also inaccurate: transmittance should depend on the spatially varying projected Gaussian alpha, rather than only the scalar opacity g_alpha, and the stated covariance and projection notation does not match standard 3DGS rendering. These errors make it difficult to determine precisely what was implemented.

Reproducibility is inadequate. The paper does not specify the correspondence-confidence threshold, outlier or cheirality filtering, triangulation conditioning, matching resolution, opacity initialization, scale formula or scaling coefficient, handling of spherical-harmonic coefficients, pruning rules, or several relevant optimizer settings. It merely states that scale is based on distance to a camera, while the supplementary notation introduces an undefined scaling factor. The claimed early-stopping mechanism is likewise not described; the experiments appear simply to stop at 5K iterations.

Several headline claims overstate the evidence. On Mip-NeRF360, the best proposed variant does not surpass 3DGS-MCMC in PSNR or SSIM, and the plain 30K variant is slower than the retrained 3DGS baseline on Mip-NeRF360 and Deep Blending. The statement that the method uses 'only half' the splats is not generally supported: plain EDGS uses 1.9M versus 2.8M on Mip-NeRF360, while the Taming combination uses the same 3.2M splats as Taming.

The efficiency comparison is not sufficiently controlled. Some baseline numbers come from different GPUs, initialization costs are handled differently across categories, integer-minute timings provide little resolution, and there is no breakdown of dense matching, triangulation, and optimization costs. Peak memory and inference/rendering speed are also not compared across methods.

One reported result is highly anomalous: the plain method obtains 0.998 SSIM on the Mip-NeRF360 counter scene despite PSNR 29.49 and LPIPS 0.169, far above its Taming variant's 0.925 SSIM. This value materially raises the nine-scene mean to the reported 0.840, yet it is neither explained nor independently supported. Together with the absence of repeated runs or uncertainty estimates, this weakens confidence in the quantitative conclusions.

The method is essentially dense matching followed by classical triangulation and standard 3DGS optimization. Applying this pipeline to eliminate densification is useful, but the technical novelty is moderate, and the manuscript does not sufficiently establish what is new beyond adopting a stronger dense geometric initialization.

Presentation problems—including grammatical errors, inconsistent notation, and imprecise phrases such as placing a Gaussian at every 'meaningful location'—are frequent. These are secondary to the correctness and reproducibility concerns above, but they further obscure an already underspecified method.

strengths: The core idea is simple, plausible, and useful: triangulating dense pretrained 2D correspondences to initialize Gaussian positions and colors directly addresses the slow discover-and-densify behavior of standard 3DGS without modifying its renderer or objective.

The empirical evidence is broad for this problem setting, covering all 13 standard scenes from Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending, with PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, runtime, Gaussian count, qualitative comparisons, and per-scene results. The results support a favorable quality-efficiency tradeoff. On Mip-NeRF360, the 5K-step Taming variant reaches 0.825 SSIM/0.195 LPIPS in 6 minutes versus 0.820/0.207 in 14 minutes for Taming 3DGS. At 30K steps, the 3DGS variant improves over the retrained 3DGS baseline from 0.816/0.215 to 0.840/0.175 SSIM/LPIPS while using 1.9M rather than 2.8M Gaussians.

Combining the initialization with both standard 3DGS and Taming 3DGS provides useful evidence that the contribution is reasonably orthogonal to optimization and rasterization improvements rather than being tied to one implementation.

The ablations are informative: RoMa is compared with LoFTR, DKM, RAFT, and depth initialization; densification is enabled and disabled; sensitivity to reference-view and match counts is examined; and controlled coordinate/color perturbations test robustness. Visual results also consistently show sharper fine structure.
weaknesses: Some headline claims are broader than the results. The 30K model does not uniformly outperform every quality-focused method on Mip-NeRF360: 3DGS-MCMC has slightly higher PSNR and SSIM than the reported EDGS variants. Likewise, the claim of using "half the splats" depends on comparison with the originally reported 3DGS count; the reduction relative to the stronger retrained baseline is about 32%, and the Taming combination uses the same reported Gaussian count as Taming alone.

The explanatory Gaussian-motion experiment is underspecified. Standard 3DGS creates and removes Gaussians during densification, so identities and trajectories are not directly comparable to the fixed initialized population. The paper does not explain which baseline Gaussians enter Figure 5 or how split, cloned, and pruned Gaussians are handled, weakening the claimed 30-50x path-length interpretation.

Reproducibility details are incomplete. The manuscript does not give the correspondence-confidence threshold, explicit scale-initialization formula and coefficient, invalid-triangulation filtering rules, or sufficiently precise sampling/pruning settings. These choices can materially affect both initial Gaussian count and reconstruction quality.

The evaluation does not report repeated runs or uncertainty. Several comparisons involve small metric differences, such as LPIPS 0.174 versus 0.176 on Mip-NeRF360, so the significance of fine-grained rankings is unclear.

Runtime comparisons are not entirely controlled: some unavailable baselines are quoted from A6000 or RTX 3090 experiments, while EDGS uses an A100. Although the authors clearly annotate this and include their matching cost, conclusions based on exact cross-method speed ratios should be qualified.

The method depends on calibrated, densely overlapping views and a substantial pretrained matcher. Failure behavior under pose error, sparse or weak overlap, repetitive texture, and dynamic content is not quantitatively studied. The extreme-viewpoint claim is supported by only one qualitative example and no geometric or out-of-distribution metric.

The conceptual novelty is moderate because dense matching followed by calibrated triangulation is classical; the main contribution is its effective application as a no-densification 3DGS initialization. Nevertheless, the consistent empirical gains and practical compatibility make the overall case lean toward acceptance.

strengths: The central idea is simple, original enough, and practically useful: dense 2D correspondences are triangulated to front-load scene coverage, replacing iterative 3DGS densification without changing the downstream optimizer.

The empirical gains are substantial, particularly for perceptual quality. On Mip-NeRF360, EDGS obtains LPIPS 0.141 versus 0.176 for the strongest listed baseline; corresponding improvements also appear on Tanks & Temples (0.132 versus 0.156) and when EDGS initializes AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, and Taming-3DGS.

The evaluation covers three standard dense-view benchmarks, early-stopping settings, sparse-view reconstruction, multiple matching backbones, component ablations, initialization alternatives, sensitivity studies, and per-scene results. Including initialization in EDGS runtime makes the reported convergence evidence more credible.

The analysis of Gaussian trajectories and the dense-COLMAP control help substantiate the proposed mechanism: the benefit is not merely a larger initial point set, and the initialized Gaussians require markedly less coordinate movement. Qualitative results are consistent with the strong LPIPS improvements.
weaknesses: The mathematical specification contains consequential errors or ambiguities. In Eqs. 6–7, the stated homogeneous least-squares problem has b=0 and no scale constraint, so its minimizer is the zero vector rather than a valid triangulated point. Equation 1 also composites with products of opacity parameters rather than the preceding projected Gaussian contributions, and Eq. 15 accesses g(T+1). These may be notation mistakes, but as written the method is not technically reproducible.

The sampling formulation is insufficiently precise. The product of two uniform distributions over thresholded sets mainly implements intersection, not graded confidence or reprojection weighting, while the cross-view “union” used to define the global distribution is not a probability operation. It is therefore unclear how duplicates, normalization, and allocation across reference views are actually handled.

Important implementation details remain unspecified despite the supplement: initial rotation, opacity, exact scale proportionality, pruning schedule, invalid/behind-camera triangulation handling, and the camera-matrix distance convention. No variability across runs or scenes is reported, so the reliability of smaller PSNR/SSIM differences cannot be assessed.

The efficiency and generality claims should be qualified. EDGS uses a pretrained dense matcher, known COLMAP camera parameters, up to 180 reference views, and roughly 15 GB initialization memory. Comparisons do not consistently include preprocessing for competing pipelines, and the strongest evidence is on the same three canonical 3DGS datasets; robustness to inaccurate poses, weak overlap, repetitive texture, and larger scenes is not established. Nevertheless, these limitations do not outweigh the well-supported perceptual-quality and convergence contribution.

strengths: The central idea is simple but useful: replacing iterative 3DGS densification with dense correspondence-based triangulation directly addresses a real optimization bottleneck and requires no change to the downstream 3DGS optimizer.

The empirical gains are substantial across all three standard benchmark families. For example, on Mip-NeRF360, densification-free EDGS improves LPIPS from 0.215 for the retrained 3DGS baseline and 0.176 for 3DGS-MCMC to 0.141, while using fewer final Gaussians than these baselines.

The early-stopping results support the convergence claim: the 10K-step model obtains 0.154 LPIPS in 12 minutes, outperforming the reported efficiency-oriented alternatives, and initialization time is included in EDGS runtimes.

The evaluation covers reconstruction quality, runtime, model size, alternative matchers, sparse-view inputs, noise sensitivity, hyperparameter sensitivity, and integration with three adaptive density-control methods. The latter consistently improves all reported metrics without increasing the final Gaussian count, providing evidence that the initialization is broadly useful.

Ablations indicate that correspondence confidence, reprojection filtering, and spherical-harmonic initialization each contribute. Comparisons against random, depth-based, VGGT-based, and duplicated-COLMAP initialization help establish that the gains are not explained solely by starting with more splats.
The paper is generally clear and the qualitative results agree with the strong LPIPS improvements, particularly in fine-texture regions.
weaknesses: The triangulation derivation is technically incorrect as written. Equation 6 sets b=0 and Equation 7 minimizes ||Ax+b|| without a homogeneous-scale constraint, whose trivial solution is x=0; the stated projection-matrix dimensions also vary between the main text and notation table. A standard constrained homogeneous SVD or an explicitly derived inhomogeneous system is presumably implemented, but the manuscript does not specify a valid algorithm. This is an important reproducibility flaw, although likely correctable rather than evidence that the experiments themselves are invalid.

Several initialization details needed for faithful reproduction remain unspecified: the proportionality constant and neighborhood rule for initial Gaussian scales, initial rotations and opacities, handling of duplicate or invalid triangulations, pruning settings, random sampling seeds, and the exact camera-matrix normalization used when selecting neighbors by Frobenius distance. No repeated-run variance or uncertainty is reported despite stochastic correspondence sampling.

The spherical-harmonic construction is weakly justified. Each Gaussian reportedly has only about two observations for 16 coefficients, so the problem is severely underdetermined; describing the pseudoinverse estimate as stable is not substantiated. The DC component is then overwritten after solving, and the effect of this inconsistent construction is not separated from other initialization changes beyond an aggregate ablation.

The sampling formulation is ambiguous: products and maxima of pair-specific uniform distributions are treated as a per-image probability, followed by a set-union-style global aggregation without explicit normalization or a clear correspondence-index mapping across image pairs. The implementation description is easier to infer than the equations but still leaves edge cases unclear.

The strongest efficiency language is somewhat overstated. At full 30K training, EDGS takes 27 minutes on Mip-NeRF360 versus 26 minutes for the retrained 3DGS baseline, so the demonstrated advantage is principally faster quality convergence rather than uniformly lower end-to-end training time. Runtime comparisons also mix reproduced measurements with results from different GPUs, and preprocessing conventions are not completely uniform across methods.

Originality is moderate: dense matching followed by calibrated-view triangulation is classical, and the contribution is chiefly its sampling and application as a 3DGS initialization. The strong results make this worthwhile, but the paper should position the contribution as an effective systems/optimization insight rather than a fundamentally new geometric method.

Per-scene tables are provided only for EDGS variants, not the principal baselines, and the paper reports no statistical variation. Consequently, it is difficult to determine whether gains are consistent scene by scene or concentrated in particular scenes, especially for the smaller Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending evaluations.

strengths: The central idea is simple, original, and practically meaningful: dense multi-view correspondences provide an informed 3DGS initialization that can replace incremental densification without changing the downstream optimizer.

The empirical case is strong across the standard Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending benchmarks. EDGS obtains particularly large LPIPS improvements—for example, 0.141 versus 0.215 for the retrained 3DGS baseline on Mip-NeRF360—while generally using fewer final Gaussians.

The paper evaluates both quality and efficiency. Initialization time is included for EDGS, early-stopped 5K/10K results demonstrate faster convergence, and competing methods are mostly rerun on the same A100 hardware, making the central efficiency claim reasonably well supported.

The analysis goes beyond aggregate benchmarks: component ablations, four correspondence backbones, sensitivity experiments, alternative initializations, Gaussian trajectory measurements, sparse-view tests, per-scene results, and qualitative comparisons collectively support the proposed explanation.

Compatibility experiments with AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, and Taming 3DGS show that the initialization can also complement adaptive density control rather than serving only as a specialized replacement. This increases the method's potential usefulness.

The manuscript is generally clear and visually persuasive. The method has an understandable motivation, and the supplement reports initialization runtime, memory consumption, thresholds, sample counts, and evaluation protocols.
weaknesses: A material limitation is the dependence on a pretrained dense matcher and calibrated, sufficiently overlapping views. Although several matchers and a sparse-view setting are tested, the paper does not systematically evaluate difficult correspondence regimes such as repetitive or textureless regions, severe illumination changes, or very wide baselines. Thus, the robustness and generality claims are broader than the presented evidence.

Reproducibility remains incomplete. Important initialization choices are underspecified, including the exact formula and constant for setting Gaussian scale from camera distance, initial opacity and rotation, pruning settings, and the precise camera-distance computation used to choose neighbors. No code or release commitment is stated in the manuscript.

The spherical-harmonic initialization is weakly justified technically. Each Gaussian typically has only two color observations for 16 basis coefficients, so the pseudoinverse solution is severely underdetermined. The ablation shows empirical benefit, but the paper does not analyze conditioning, regularization, or why this minimum-norm solution should generalize to unseen directions.

Several equations contain inconsistencies that should be corrected. Projection matrices are described as 4×3 in the main derivation but 3×4 in the notation table; the rendering equation appears to use opacity both inside sigma and again in transmittance; and the sampling distributions and their multiplication/max aggregation are not defined with enough precision to reproduce the actual sampler. These look primarily expositional, but they obscure technical verification.

The strongest quality comparisons report only single aggregate results, without multiple seeds or uncertainty. This is less concerning for the large LPIPS gains, but some PSNR/SSIM differences are small enough that variability would matter.

Some claims are overstated relative to the evidence. For example, 'state-of-the-art performance' is based on a selected set of 3DGS baselines, and the extreme-viewpoint claim is supported mainly by one qualitative example without held-out quantitative evaluation. These do not invalidate the core contribution but should be narrowed.
